**Considering mirror views**

I’m thinking about how front and back mirrors can make views appear opposite due to the way we see from different angles. It's interesting to consider how paired side slots and mounting holes play a role in this. I wonder how this might affect installation or functionality. There's a lot to think about when it comes to mirrors and their alignment, and I want to ensure I understand it well!
**Analyzing coordinate surfaces**

I'm considering the x/y coordinates, where the x could be vertical and the base length is likely 168 while the height is 180. It suggests that some surfaces are lower near the base. The coordinates for faces indicate various regions connected and disconnected, with some surfaces possibly being part of the head and others being internal fork surfaces. I need to carefully map these without duplicates, ensuring all faces from 0-66 are covered. This could be a detailed task!
**Mapping surface codes**

I'm planning to categorize the surfaces into major and minor, with about 37 major surfaces and the rest being minor fillets and chamfers. I want to create face codes starting from 0000 sequentially to 38, while ensuring adjacent surfaces are properly ordered. For S1, I’ll identify the top and bottom of the base and clarify the positions of various elements. In S2, I’ll mark the major faces and ensure the layout is logical, despite some disconnected holes. Walking through these surfaces will help!

part.name: Pedestal-mounted fork bracket with threaded top boss
part.description: Single-piece mechanical mounting bracket comprising an elongated two-hole base plate, a thick asymmetric upright web with an open fork-like cavity, paired obround side pockets, a reduced-thickness upper head, a transverse locating hole, and a reinforced threaded boss on top. The STEP model is one solid with 67 B-rep faces and an overall bounding box of 168 x 180 x 60 mm.
part.symmetry_note: The base plate, top boss, transverse head hole, and paired side pockets are approximately symmetric about the thickness mid-plane z=-21 mm. The upright profile is strongly asymmetric along the base length because of the open fork cavity and curved load path. Front and back appearances are approximately mirrored.

Section.name: Base mounting plate
Section.function intent: Mounts the bracket to a machine frame or foundation and establishes the primary positional datum for the upright structure.
Section.physical behavior: The broad underside reacts clamp preload and service loads into the supporting structure. The two spaced holes resist translation and in-plane rotation, while the plate width and rounded ends distribute bearing and bending stresses.
Section.geometry: A long rectangular plate of approximately 168 mm length, 60 mm width, and 15 mm thickness. It has semicircular or quarter-cylindrical corner transitions and two cylindrical through holes positioned near opposite longitudinal ends.
Section.location: Lowest section of the part, extending across the full length and width.

major_faces.name: Base upper deck
major_faces.description: Large horizontal upper surface at y=15 mm supporting the upright and surrounding both mounting holes.

major_faces.name: Base underside
major_faces.description: Large horizontal mounting surface at y=0 mm that seats against the supporting structure.

major_faces.name: Long outer edge wall
major_faces.description: Long planar thickness wall along the z=-60 mm edge of the base.

major_faces.name: Right end wall
major_faces.description: Planar end wall at x=168 mm between the rounded base corners.

major_faces.name: Left end wall
major_faces.description: Planar end wall at x=0 mm between the rounded base corners.

major_faces.name: Right mounting-hole wall
major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall of the through mounting hole centered near x=153 mm.

major_faces.name: Left mounting-hole wall
major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall of the through mounting hole centered near x=15 mm.

Section.name: Main upright web and arched spine
Section.function intent: Carries loads between the elevated head and the mounting plate while leaving access space for a mating component in the central opening.
Section.physical behavior: Acts primarily as a thick bending web. The arched outer contour redirects force around the central opening, and the broad root transfers bending moment and shear into the base. Curved profile transitions reduce stress concentration compared with sharp re-entrant corners.
Section.geometry: A thick, vertically rising asymmetric web. Its upper portion curves laterally to support the head, while its lower portion forms one side of the fork opening. Broad front and back facets are connected by planar and cylindrical perimeter walls.
Section.location: Above the base, principally through the central and right-hand region in the front view.

major_faces.name: Primary front web facet
major_faces.description: Large planar side face at z=0 mm covering much of the upright and lower frame.

major_faces.name: Outer arched spine
major_faces.description: Large convex cylindrical patch of radius 51 mm forming the prominent curved outer load path.

major_faces.name: Upper spine transition
major_faces.description: Smaller cylindrical blend connecting the outer arch to the reduced upper structure.

major_faces.name: Outer upright wall
major_faces.description: Planar thickness wall along the outer side of the lower upright.

major_faces.name: Lower outer corner
major_faces.description: Cylindrical corner patch joining the upright perimeter to the adjacent straight wall.

major_faces.name: Primary back web facet
major_faces.description: Large planar side face at z=-42 mm forming the opposite major web surface.

major_faces.name: Inner-side upright wall
major_faces.description: Tall planar thickness wall on the opposite longitudinal side of the lower upright.

major_faces.name: Lower straight web wall
major_faces.description: Planar wall joining the lower upright profile to the nearby fork geometry.

Section.name: Open fork and central clearance cavity
features included: paired front and back cavity facets
Section.function intent: Provides an accessible receiving space for a mating shaft, link, clamp member, or workpiece while retaining it laterally with the surrounding fork structure.
Section.physical behavior: The open mouth permits lateral insertion. Concave cylindrical surfaces guide or nest a rounded mating component, while inclined and planar walls establish clearance and possible travel limits. The remaining material around the cavity carries load as two connected arms.
Section.geometry: A large, irregular open cavity cut into the middle of the upright. It combines a broad concave cylindrical arc, a smaller transition radius, inclined planar walls, short ledges, and mirrored depth faces on opposite sides.
Section.location: Central-lower region of the upright, opening toward the left in the front view.

major_faces.name: Front lower cavity facet
major_faces.description: Planar recessed side facet at z=-12 mm near the lower portion of the fork.

major_faces.name: Front entry-radius wall
major_faces.description: Cylindrical patch forming one rounded end of the cavity entry.

major_faces.name: Front inclined cavity wall
major_faces.description: Inclined planar wall leading from the lower fork arm into the central opening.

major_faces.name: Central inclined guide wall
major_faces.description: Long inclined planar wall defining a principal internal boundary of the fork.

major_faces.name: Upper concave transition
major_faces.description: Concave cylindrical patch of radius 15 mm blending the inclined wall into the main cavity arc.

major_faces.name: Main concave cavity arc
major_faces.description: Large cylindrical inner surface of radius 27 mm that guides or clears a rounded mating part.

major_faces.name: Front cavity stop ledge
major_faces.description: Short planar ledge terminating part of the lower fork opening.

major_faces.name: Back lower cavity facet
major_faces.description: Opposite planar recessed side facet at z=-30 mm.

major_faces.name: Back entry-radius wall
major_faces.description: Cylindrical patch forming the opposite-depth rounded cavity entry.

major_faces.name: Back cavity stop ledge
major_faces.description: Planar ledge corresponding to the opposite side of the lower fork opening.

Section.name: Upper head block
Section.function intent: Provides an elevated, stiff interface for the threaded boss and a transverse pin or locating feature.
Section.physical behavior: The box-like head resists local bearing and bending around the transverse hole and distributes boss loads into the arched spine. Reduced thickness gives side clearance, while filleted lower transitions suppress peak stresses.
Section.geometry: An approximately rectangular upper block, narrower through the thickness than the lower web. It has broad parallel side facets, straight side walls, rounded upper edges, a small transverse cylindrical hole, and blended transitions into the spine.
Section.location: Uppermost rectangular body directly below the threaded boss.

major_faces.name: Head front facet
major_faces.description: Large planar face at z=-12 mm forming one broad side of the upper head.

major_faces.name: Head left side wall
major_faces.description: Planar wall along x=46.5 mm bounding one side of the head.

major_faces.name: Head upper end wall
major_faces.description: Upper planar wall of the head surrounding the transition into the boss support.

major_faces.name: Boss support seat
major_faces.description: Planar annular or split seat at y=153 mm beneath the central boss bore.

major_faces.name: Head right side wall
major_faces.description: Planar wall along x=88.5 mm bounding the opposite side of the head.

major_faces.name: Head back facet
major_faces.description: Large planar face at z=-30 mm forming the opposite broad side of the upper head.

major_faces.name: Transverse-hole right segment
major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall segment of the small transverse locating or pin hole on one side.

major_faces.name: Transverse-hole left segment
major_faces.description: Cylindrical wall segment of the same transverse hole on the opposite side.

Section.name: Paired obround side pockets
Section.function intent: Provides local clearance, mass reduction, tool access, or a recessed interface on both sides of the lower upright.
Section.physical behavior: The shallow pockets remove material away from the principal outer load path while retaining a central core. Rounded ends reduce stress concentration relative to rectangular slots and can guide an obround mating feature.
Section.geometry: Two matching shallow obround recesses located on opposite thickness faces. Each recess has a flat floor, two straight side walls, and two semicylindrical end walls with approximately 9 mm radius.
Section.location: Lower upright, one pocket visible from the front and the matching pocket visible from the back.

major_faces.name: Front pocket floor
major_faces.description: Flat obround pocket floor at z=-10 mm.

major_faces.name: Front pocket upper end
major_faces.description: Semicylindrical end wall forming one rounded end of the front pocket.

major_faces.name: Front pocket lower end
major_faces.description: Semicylindrical end wall forming the opposite rounded end of the front pocket.

major_faces.name: Back pocket floor
major_faces.description: Flat obround pocket floor at z=-32 mm.

major_faces.name: Back pocket lower end
major_faces.description: Semicylindrical end wall forming one rounded end of the back pocket.

major_faces.name: Back pocket upper end
major_faces.description: Semicylindrical end wall forming the opposite rounded end of the back pocket.

Section.name: Threaded top boss and reinforcement collar
Section.function intent: Provides a coaxial threaded attachment point for a bolt, stud, actuator, fitting, or adjustment screw at the top of the bracket.
Section.physical behavior: The cylindrical boss supplies thread engagement length and reacts axial clamp force and transverse shear. The enlarged collar spreads these loads into the upper head, while the toroidal and spline blends reduce stress concentration at the boss root. The top chamfer assists fastener entry.
Section.geometry: A vertical hollow cylindrical boss centered on the upper head. It includes an internal cylindrical bore, an external cylinder, a conical top chamfer, a flat annular top face, and a rounded reinforcement collar transitioning into the head.
Section.location: Centered on the top surface of the upper head.

major_faces.name: Right collar seat
major_faces.description: Planar shoulder facet on one side of the boss reinforcement collar.

major_faces.name: Right toroidal collar
major_faces.description: Toroidal root-blend patch spreading boss load into the upper head.

major_faces.name: Boss outer cylinder
major_faces.description: Principal cylindrical outside wall of the elevated attachment boss.

major_faces.name: Boss lead-in chamfer
major_faces.description: Conical chamfer around the upper end of the boss.

major_faces.name: Boss top annulus
major_faces.description: Flat annular top face surrounding the central threaded bore.

major_faces.name: Threaded-bore envelope
major_faces.description: Cylindrical B-rep surface representing the central bore; rendered thread detail is not individually resolved in the report.

major_faces.name: Left collar seat
major_faces.description: Planar shoulder facet on the opposite side of the boss reinforcement collar.
